chunks: He said: Abu Ghalib al-Zurari reported to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran narrated to us, he said: Safwan narrated to us, from Seif al-Tammar, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), he said: I heard him saying:

Be constant in supplication, for indeed you cannot draw near [to God] with anything like it. And do not neglect asking for a small matter because of its smallness, for the Provider of the small is also the Provider of the great.

key_terms.الدعاء: Du'a (supplication) - the act of calling upon God, considered one of the highest forms of worship
key_terms.صاحب: Provider/Master - here referring to God as the one who controls and grants both small and great matters

ai.seo_question: Why is supplication (du'a) considered the best way to draw near to God in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) instructs believers to be persistent in supplication (du'a), emphasizing that no form of worship brings one closer to God than supplication. He further advises against neglecting to ask God for small needs, reasoning that the One who provides small things is the same One who provides great things. This teaching was delivered to his companions in Medina, reflecting the Imam's characteristic emphasis on the accessibility and intimacy of the relationship between the servant and God.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. He said: Abu Ghalib al-Zurari reported to me from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who reported from Abdul Rehman ibn Abu Najran who reported from Safwan, from Seif al-Tammar, who reported that Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad (A.S.) said:

"Be supplicating constantly, for there is nothing like it to take you nearer (to Allah). And do not avoid asking for small matters because of its smallness, for the provider of the small is also the provider of the big."
